title: Slices
summary: &str and &[T] are borrowed views into existing data - no ownership, no allocation.
lecture: A slice is a fat pointer: an address plus a length, viewing a contiguous run of data someone else owns. &str views string data (whether it lives in a String, a literal, or another slice); &[T] views array or Vec elements the same way.

Because a slice borrows rather than owns, producing one is free - no allocation, no copying. Methods like split_whitespace() on &str hand back sub-slices of the original data, which is what makes zero-copy string processing possible.

In signatures, slices are the accepting types: &[String] takes a &Vec<String>, a fixed-size array, or a sub-range; &str takes any string-shaped thing. The owning types (Vec, String) belong in parameters only when the function genuinely needs to keep or consume the data.

example.caption: The slice parameter reads the Vec's data without taking it.
